DEFINITION · qeva:1:theorem@1

Theorem

A theorem is a statement accompanied by a valid derivation from declared assumptions in a declared system.

editoriallogic · proof

PLAIN

The idea

A theorem is a statement accompanied by a valid derivation from declared assumptions in a declared system.

EXACT

The compact statement

P is a theorem of T relative to proof calculus S when T ⊢ₛ P. The claim is incomplete unless T, S, and the reading of P are recoverable.

EXAMPLE

The Pythagorean theorem is a family of precisely stated results whose assumptions depend on the geometry used.

BOUNDARY / CAVEAT

The label theorem records derivational status, not importance or universal truth across all models.

ASSUMPTIONS

  • The declared formal or mathematical theory context is fixed.
